I've always had a bit of a fascination with Anne Boleyn and how she pretty much single handedly changed the entire course of British history

The big things would be that she was the cause for Henry VIII's divorce and the break between England and the Catholic Church, and her daughter was of course Elizabeth I, both of which had enormous impacts on what England would become.

Then there are seemingly smaller effects (ie Elizabeth refusing to get married, had she married her reign would've undoubtedly been very different, or even some of the actions and decisions of her half sister "Bloody Mary"), that occurred as a result of the few years of influence she had and her execution.

Had she not been around or just agreed to sleep with Henry a few times and moved on, he very likely would've stayed married to Catherine of Aragon, who knows how long England would've remained a Catholic country, Elizabeth I probably wouldn't have existed and if she did I seriously doubt she would've been Queen or even acknowledged, and who knows how many other things would've been different as a direct or indirect result. Hell, Elizabeth I having no direct heirs and the throne going to James I is what led to Great Britain.

I noticed some posts today, and an on-going trend of posts; there is a constant comparison to reddit, and I think this is terrible. Many of us left reddit because we disagreed with the philisophical shifts from free speech to hive-mind filtered speech, and no one is willing to really admit that by recreating that environment, we are inviting the very parts we don't like.

I get that currently, a big issue with reddit is the management, but that management has been a long time brewing because of community sway, and building the same communities within voat will inevitably lead to the same fate as reddit. So far, the only difference we really have is management, but our culture is still the same.

But this brings me to my main question - what's the end game of voat? Are we doomed to follow reddit, digg, and others that have boomed and crashed before us? What makes us different (here's a hint, we are starting at the same square one that reddit started at)? Why would anyone pick voat over reddit? What will keep this community thriving through free speech oppression? What safe guards do we have in place for when our freedom becomes priviledge rather than a right?
